concepts.name: Classification of Floods: Types and Triggering Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Distinction between riverine, flash, coastal, urban, and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) — definitions and causes
UPSC trap: Flash floods vs. riverine floods — speed of onset, predictability, and management differences
Pluvial (surface water) floods vs. fluvial floods — often confused; pluvial not dependent on proximity to water body
Role of cloud bursts, cyclones, dam breaks, and snowmelt as distinct triggering mechanisms for different flood types

concepts.name: Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs): Mechanism and Indian Context
key_dimensions: Formation of glacial lakes (moraine-dammed, ice-dammed) and conditions triggering outburst
Indian vulnerability: Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim — Teesta GLOF 2023 as a case study
UPSC trap: GLOFs are NOT seasonal like riverine floods; they are sudden and climate-change-amplified
ISRO and NRSC's role in glacial lake inventory and early warning — distinction from IMD's role

concepts.name: Urban Floods: Causes, Characteristics, and Management Challenges
key_dimensions: Imperviousness of urban surfaces, encroachment of natural drains, inadequate stormwater systems as root causes
Mumbai 2005, Chennai 2015, Bengaluru 2022 — pattern of repeat urban flooding despite warnings
UPSC trap: Urban floods are primarily a governance/planning failure, not purely a natural event — role of Master Plans and Floor Space Index
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines on urban flood management: blue-green infrastructure, sponge city concept

concepts.name: Flood Hazard Zonation and Mapping in India
key_dimensions: Flood plain zoning: Zone A (active flood plain) vs. Zone B (flood plain proper) — prohibited and regulated land uses
Rashtriya Barh Ayog (National Flood Commission) 1980 recommendations on flood plain zoning — largely unimplemented
UPSC trap: Flood Hazard Atlas vs. Flood Plain Zoning — mapping is done but statutory zoning laws adopted by very few states
Role of National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) and Bhuvan portal in near-real-time flood inundation mapping

concepts.name: India's Flood-Prone Geography: Regional Patterns and Paradoxes
key_dimensions: Brahmaputra basin (Assam), Ganga-Mahanadi plains, peninsular rivers — distinct flood behaviour and seasonality
UPSC trap: Rajasthan and Vidarbha experience droughts AND floods in same or alternate years — concept of 'flood-drought continuum'
Role of physiography: Himalayan rivers (high sediment load, shifting channels) vs. peninsular rivers (hard rock, rapid runoff)
India accounts for ~20% of global flood deaths despite advanced warning — paradox of persistent vulnerability

concepts.name: Structural Flood Management Measures: Embankments and Dams
key_dimensions: Embankments (levees): mechanism of protection, false sense of security, and embankment-failure floods (Bihar)
UPSC trap: Embankments often INCREASE flood risk over time by raising riverbed through sediment deposition — Farakka Barrage controversy
Dams and reservoirs for flood moderation: distinction between flood control storage and dead storage
Interlinking of Rivers (ILR) project as a structural flood management strategy — arguments for and against, Ken-Betwa link

concepts.name: Non-Structural Flood Management: Early Warning, Zoning, and Insurance
key_dimensions: Central Water Commission (CWC) flood forecasting network: coverage, lead time, and accuracy limitations
UPSC trap: CWC provides flood forecasts only for specific gauge stations — gap between forecast and community-level warning dissemination
Flood plain zoning legislation: Model Bill 1975 — why most states have NOT enacted it (political economy of encroachment)
National Crop Insurance and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana — coverage gaps for flood losses in non-agricultural assets

concepts.name: Institutional Framework for Flood Management in India
key_dimensions: Constitutional position: Water is a State subject (Entry 17, List II) — Centre's limited direct authority over flood management
UPSC trap: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) sets guidelines but State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) implement — coordination failure
Central Water Commission vs. National Water Development Agency vs. Brahmaputra Board — overlapping mandates
Role of Army, NDRF, and SDRF in flood response — distinction between NDRF (central) and SDRF (state-funded)

concepts.name: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF): Roles and Limitations
key_dimensions: NDRF: statutory body under Disaster Management Act 2005, 16 battalions, deployment authority vests with NDMA/Home Ministry
UPSC trap: SDRF is NOT a statutory force like NDRF — it is a fund-based mechanism; states raise their own rescue forces separately
Pre-positioning of NDRF during monsoon season — proactive vs. reactive deployment distinction
Limitations: NDRF cannot be pre-positioned in every vulnerable district; last-mile connectivity challenges in Himalayan floods

concepts.name: Disaster Management Act 2005: Flood-Specific Provisions and Gaps
key_dimensions: Hierarchy: NDMA → SDMA → DDMA — roles in flood preparedness, response, and mitigation
UPSC trap: The Act mandates 'mitigation' but flood plain zoning (the most effective mitigation tool) requires separate state legislation
National Disaster Mitigation Fund vs. National Disaster Response Fund — purposes, sources, and utilization rules
2005 Act does not cover slow-onset disasters well — gap in addressing prolonged riverine flooding in Assam/Bihar

concepts.name: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) and Flood Management
key_dimensions: Four priorities: understanding risk, governance, investment in DRR, build-back-better — how they apply to flood management
UPSC trap: Sendai Framework is NOT legally binding — it is a voluntary agreement, unlike Paris Agreement which has NDC commitments
Targets: Reduce disaster mortality, reduce economic losses, increase access to early warning systems by 2030
India's alignment: National DRR Plan 2016 maps Sendai targets to Indian context — distinction between plan and implementation

concepts.name: Role of Wetlands and Floodplains as Natural Flood Buffers
key_dimensions: Floodplains as natural retention areas: encroachment reduces flood attenuation capacity — Loktak Lake, Kolleru, Chilika examples
UPSC trap: Ramsar sites have conservation obligations but NO legal prohibition on encroachment under Indian law — gap between international commitment and domestic law
Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017: restrictions on reclamation — enforcement challenges
Ecosystem-based adaptation (EbA) for floods: mangroves as coastal flood buffers, urban wetlands as stormwater sponges

concepts.name: Climate Change and Intensification of Flood Events in India
key_dimensions: IPCC AR6 findings: increased frequency of extreme precipitation events, accelerated glacial melt — compound flood risks
UPSC trap: Climate change does NOT cause floods directly — it alters the frequency, intensity, and spatial distribution of flood-triggering events
Western Ghats and Northeast India: already high rainfall zones experiencing more intense cloudburst events
Loss and Damage framework (COP27): floods as key drivers of climate-induced loss — relevance for India's climate diplomacy

concepts.name: Transboundary Flood Management: India's Challenges with Riparian Neighbours
key_dimensions: India-Nepal: Kosi Agreement 1954/2008 — Kosi embankment breach 2008, data sharing gaps, political tensions over barrages
UPSC trap: India receives flood waters FROM Nepal (upper riparian) but is accused of flooding Bangladesh (lower riparian) — dual riparian position
India-Bangladesh: Farakka Barrage controversy — upstream water retention causing downstream flooding in Bangladesh
Brahmaputra: China's dam-building in Tibet (upstream) — lack of data-sharing agreement; India's vulnerability to artificial floods

concepts.name: Flood Relief, Compensation, and Post-Disaster Recovery Framework
key_dimensions: State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF): 75:25 Centre-State funding ratio (90:10 for NE and special category states)
UPSC trap: SDRF is the PRIMARY fund for immediate relief — NDRF is supplementary and released only when state funds are exhausted
Norms for relief: SDRF has prescribed per-unit relief amounts for house damage, crop loss — often criticized as inadequate and inflation-insensitive
Build-back-better principle vs. like-for-like reconstruction — gap in India's post-flood recovery approach

concepts.name: Flood Forecasting Technology: Satellite, IoT, and AI-Based Systems
key_dimensions: CWC's Flood Forecasting Monitoring System: telemetry-based gauge stations, SMS-based alerts — coverage limited to major rivers
ISRO's SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellites for flood inundation mapping in cloud-covered conditions — operational during monsoon
UPSC trap: Google's AI-based flood forecasting (FloodHub) now covers India — private-public gap; government systems lag in hyper-local forecasting
Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and LiDAR for urban flood modelling — Smart Cities Mission and GIS integration

concepts.name: Assam-Brahmaputra Flood Problem: Structural, Ecological, and Policy Dimensions
key_dimensions: Brahmaputra characteristics: one of world's highest sediment-laden rivers, braided channel, earthquake-prone catchment — unique flood dynamics
UPSC trap: Assam floods annually but is NOT just a monsoon problem — riverbank erosion (chars) causes permanent displacement, distinct from temporary flooding
Brahmaputra Board (1980): mandate to plan and implement flood control — criticized for focusing on infrastructure over ecosystem-based solutions
Majuli island — world's largest river island, shrinking due to erosion/flooding — cultural and ecological significance in UPSC context

concepts.name: Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction (CBDRR) in Flood Contexts
key_dimensions: Participatory approaches: community flood shelters (Bangladesh model), village-level flood task forces — India's adoption under NDMA guidelines
UPSC trap: CBDRR is mentioned in Sendai Framework and India's DRR Plan but has NO dedicated funding stream — absorbed under general SDRF/MGNREGS
Traditional/indigenous flood management knowledge: Zabo system (Nagaland), Bamboo check dams — recognition in national policy vs. ground reality
Role of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in flood preparedness — 73rd Amendment and disaster management — functional devolution gap

concepts.name: Sponge City and Blue-Green Infrastructure Concepts for Urban Flood Resilience
key_dimensions: Sponge city concept: urban design that absorbs, stores, and slowly releases stormwater — origin in China, adoption in Indian Smart Cities Mission
Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI): rain gardens, permeable pavements, urban wetlands, green roofs — contrast with grey infrastructure (storm drains)
UPSC trap: AMRUT 2.0 includes stormwater management but does NOT mandate BGI — gap between aspiration and regulatory requirement
Co-benefits of BGI: urban heat island reduction, biodiversity, groundwater recharge — relevance to both flood AND drought management

concepts.name: Flood Risk Index, Vulnerability Assessment, and Disaster Risk Profiling
key_dimensions: Components of flood risk: Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability − Capacity — distinction between hazard (physical) and risk (socio-physical construct)
UPSC trap: High hazard ≠ High risk — Assam has higher hazard but Kerala 2018 had higher risk due to exposure and governance failure
District Disaster Management Plans (DDMPs) mandated under DM Act 2005 — quality and updating status a persistent gap
National Disaster Risk Index (NDRI) by NDMA — ranks districts by multi-hazard risk; flood being the highest contributor to composite risk score
